test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 6 Oct 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A shopkeeper finds that when he sells one kind of rice at Rs 50 per kg, he loses 20%. when he sells another kind of rice at Rs 72 per kg, he gains 20%. If he mixes them in the ratio 3 : 2 and sells the mixture at Rs 64 per kg., then what is his ‘overall gain percentage (correct to one decimal place)?
solution:
**Calculations:**

SP of rice 1 = Rs. 50/kg

Thus, CP of rice 1 = 50 /0.8 = Rs.62.5/kg

SP of rice 2 = Rs. 72 /kg

and CP of rice 2 = 72 /1.2 = Rs.60/kg

CP of the mixture

⇒ 3 × 62.5 + 2 × 60

⇒ Rs.187.5 + 120

⇒ Rs. 307.5 for 5 kg

so CP of mixture = 61.5 /kg

And SP of the mixture = 64/kg

gain%

⇒ (64 - 61.5)/61/5 × 100

 = 4.06 % = 4.1% 

**Hence, The Required gain is 4.1%.**
